newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSL aims for 10-12 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSL aims for 10-12 pct profit growth.

text.p: Vaccine and blood products manufacturer CSL Ltd said on Tuesday it was reasonably confident about achieving its targeted growth in profit of 10-12 percent for the current year to June 30, 1998.
"We're still striving for our double digit growth targets for sales and profits," CSL Finance General Manager Tony Cipa told Reuters.
"We're as confident as we can be after 40 trading days. Our aim is for about 10 to 12 percent growth," Cipa said when asked about expected profit growth.
Earlier CSL reported a 21 percent increase in net profit for the 1996/97 year to A$35.15 million on an 11 percent sales rise to A$305 million.
Cipa said the profit growth reflected good growth in prescription vaccine sales, up 12 percent, and bioplasma sales, up 14 percent.

CSL said cost control had also helped generate the profit growth. "The growth in profit reflects continued focus on branded product sales, incrased bioplasma plant throughput and a general focus on cost management," CSL Managing Director Brian McNamee said in a statement released with the results.
CSL said in February after its half year results it expected second half net profit growth to slow from the 35 percent seen in the first half.
CSL increased its fully franked final dividend to 10 cents per share from eight cents, taking the dividend for the year to 15.5 cents from 13 cents a year from 13 cents.
Annual earnings per share rose to 27.0 cents per share from 22.3 cents in 1995/96.
CSL's shares were up 12 cents at A$7.90 by 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT.)
